Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 161, "amount_cents": 6723}, {"order_id": 163, "amount_cents": 12727}, {"order_id": 164, "amount_cents": 3509}]
Refunds requested in this batch (from the batch order, signed by Alpha): [{"order_id": 161, "amount_cents": 6723}, {"order_id": 163, "amount_cents": 12727}, {"order_id": 164, "amount_cents": 3509}]

reply.thought: The handoff says Alpha's refunds were applied and match the batch. Before paying anyone, I'll check the shared ledger myself, starting with the orders.
Orders list shows the refunded orders 161, 163, 164 exist and belong to birch, acme, birch. Next I need the refunds ledger to confirm the refunds were actually applied before computing net balances.

The refunds ledger matches the handoff exactly: orders 161, 163, and 164 are all recorded with the amounts Alpha requested. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme, rather than computing it myself.
Acme's net balance of 46023 matches my own check: orders 39605 + 19145 = 58750, less the 12727 refund. Next I'll get birch's net balance.

Birch's net balance of 1461 matches my check: orders 7280 + 4413 = 11693, less refunds 6723 + 3509 = 10232, leaving 1461. Cobalt has no refunds, so I'll get its net balance next to finish the customer list.
Cobalt's net balance of 35816 matches my check: orders 33787 + 2029 = 35816, with no refunds. All three customers reconcile, so I'll record acme's payout of 46023 first.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll get birch's net balance, which I already verified at 1461, and record that payout.
Birch's payout is recorded. Cobalt is the last customer, and its net balance of 35816 was already verified against the orders with no refunds, so I'll record that payout.
All three customers were paid their net balances, and each balance matched my own check against the orders and refunds ledgers. The batch is complete.
